tag: Episode 51S · The Spring We Chose to Stay
title: The One Who Stays

beats.t: Yeoni's finger touched the moonlit World Tree card. The entire square drew a light breath, and the cherry-blossom view through the open door quietly receded.
[ Choice complete · Stay in the world of fortune ]
I'll stay here. Not to run away. I want to live what comes next with the people I protected, in the world I changed.
Then I'll stay too. This time, not because of guardian regulations. I choose as Park Byeongha.
The light unraveling Neo's body stopped. A white cat's tail overlapped him like a mirage, then the heartbeat of the human Park Byeongha grew clear again.
Yeoni, I'll return. There are debts to face and people to apologize to there.
Go and live, not just repay. Put off living until everything's repaid, and that's another ledger.
Yes. This time, I'll write a line of my own life every day. I'll remember that returning isn't only settling accounts.
Yeoni opened the yellow umbrella and placed it in Seo Hanbi's hand. Its shaft, wrapped in three layers of tape, was warm between two worlds.
Wait. Take this to reality. The first line of my new song. No copyright yet, so listen all you want.
The twenty-third door connects rather than closes. You can send news once a month.
Then I can write Mom too. Not as a daughter who vanished, but one who built a home in another world.
Let's write the first letter together. Can't have you impulsively giving a star rating first.
Why are you proofreading my letter? Besides, Mom already knows my rating habit.
Seo Hanbi laughed, a laugh unseen in the first spring. Umbrella in hand, she stood before reality's cherry-blossom door.
See you in the next rain. I'll tilt the umbrella then.
After the door closed, one yellow ray remained in the air. Not a severed path, but a promise open like a door.
All right. Goodbyes done. Everyone staying, eat first. Save the world then starve, and we'll lose all dignity.
Moka spun his pan. Vegetables and flames bounced to the beat. Smiling, Yeoni set plates on the table.
Your Four Pillars have found a place in this world now too. Fortune didn't choose an address. A person did.
Here too, I'll have to get up in the morning, work, argue, apologize. That's why I stayed. Life goes on here.
You understand well. I'll wake you at seven tomorrow. Staying in the world of fortune doesn't abolish lateness.
Considering undoing my choice.
Everyone laughed. Moonlight fell through the World Tree's leaves. Beneath it, Yeoni called this place home for the first time.
The square after the farewell was quiet but not empty. The remaining companions' breaths and footsteps steadily filled every space where emptiness might enter.
Yeoni told themselves they hadn't abandoned reality, only redefined the distance between two worlds. The more they explained it, the clearer their heart became.
I'll miss things even in the life I chose. But missing them doesn't mean I chose wrong. Both feelings can coexist.
Yes. Choosing doesn't mean hating one thing in order to love another. The place you left is part of your life too.
Following the grain of the World Tree's roots, Byeongha showed them a small homesite. A waterway in view, the teahouse's moonlight within reach, the ladle a little less audible.
Sounds like you're calling my ladle noise. Expect a giant cookware set as your wedding gift.
We haven't discussed marriage! We're only looking at a homesite!
I have, in my mind. I'll say it aloud after the house is built.
The tips of Yeoni's ears reddened. Even in a flower-pig body, their expression couldn't hide. Moka lowered his microphone and smiled like an otter who'd found material for lifelong teasing.
As night deepened, news arrived from the islands they had crossed together. The eclipse had retreated. Stopped festivals resumed. Forgotten names found their owners one by one.
You already have work to do here, Yeoni. After rescue ends, recovery remains.
I can't do that alone. We'll do it together. Being the main character doesn't mean I plan to carry the whole world.
At day's end, Yeoni leaned against a World Tree root. No finished home, no settled job, no complete plan. But the earth beneath their feet was solid.
Byeongha sat beside them. They stayed silent for a long time. Enduring the same night without disappearing was their newest promise.
Let's try living here from tomorrow. Good days and bad, making them all part of my choice.
Yeoni placed a little chair before the door through which Seo Hanbi had left. When a letter arrived next month, they would sit there and read every word.
Staying didn't mean closing a door. Instead of imagining somewhere to return, Yeoni finally began writing what to do here tomorrow.
Tomorrow I'll clean the teahouse windows. The next day, visit the Island of Companions and mend broken mirrors. After that, we'll choose then.
A practical enough plan. Except I'll clean the windows. When you do it, you only add patterns.
Yeoni argued as usual. Byeongha stubbornly held his ground as usual. To both, that little disagreement felt more miraculous than a miracle.
The first spring had no tomorrow. In the second, everything had been hidden to protect tomorrow. Now they prepared for it openly, together.
Yeongnyangi, I won't forget that you came to save me. But from now on, surviving is something we'll do together.
Understood. Rescue ends after one act. Life keeps asking for each other's hands.
[ The Twenty-Third Door · Preparing the first letter · Tomorrow ]
